rubric: Editorial starting rarity for this classroom, relative to each prompt; not measured popularity. Familiar answers start at 20, then 40, 60, 80 and 100 for progressively less obvious answers. Small foundational categories use a narrower spread rather than inventing exceptional rarity. Live daily answer frequency continues to adjust these starting tiers.

categories.prompt: Name one of the three branches of the U.S. government.
categories.rationale: All three branches are foundational; judicial earns only a modest extra step, not an exceptional reward.

categories.prompt: Name a U.S. president.
categories.rationale: Widely recognized presidents start low; less recalled administrations start high.

categories.prompt: Name a right or protection in the Bill of Rights.
categories.rationale: Speech, religion, arms and self-incrimination are immediate associations; detailed trial and property protections are less obvious.

answers.label: Protection from unreasonable searches and seizures
Compensation for property taken for public use
Protection against cruel and unusual punishment

categories.prompt: Name a public office that voters can elect someone to.
categories.rationale: National offices are first associations; local and specialized offices reward broader government recall.

categories.prompt: Name an institution or office in the federal government.
categories.rationale: The branches and Congress are immediate; the EOP and agency structure are less obvious.

categories.prompt: Name a level of government in the United States.
categories.rationale: All levels are familiar, so the spread stays modest.

categories.prompt: Name a role a U.S. president performs.
categories.rationale: Chief executive and commander in chief are immediate; party and legislative roles require broader recall.

categories.prompt: Name a right listed in the Declaration of Independence.
categories.rationale: All three are familiar; the longer final ideal earns a modest extra step.

categories.prompt: Name a democratic ideal or founding principle.
categories.rationale: Natural rights and popular sovereignty are immediate; republicanism and consent require broader conceptual recall.

categories.prompt: Name a model of democracy from our course.
categories.rationale: Participatory is the most direct association; pluralist and elite models earn progressively larger climbs.

categories.prompt: Name a power or duty of the U.S. president.
categories.rationale: Signing, vetoing and command are familiar; executive agreements and special constitutional duties are less recalled.

answers.label: Give the State of the Union

categories.prompt: Name an enumerated power of Congress.
categories.rationale: Tax and war are immediate; detailed commerce, administrative and maritime powers are less obvious.

answers.label: Punish piracy and offenses on the high seas
Punish offenses against the law of nations
Grant letters of marque and reprisal
Make rules for the armed forces
Organize and call forth the militia

categories.prompt: Name part of the team that helps the president do the job.
categories.rationale: Vice president and Cabinet are immediate; staff and EOP distinguish broader institutional knowledge.

categories.prompt: Name a founding document or political text from our lessons.
categories.rationale: The Constitution, Declaration and Bill of Rights are immediate; specific Federalist essays are progressively less recalled.

categories.prompt: Name a category of government power: national, state, or shared.
categories.rationale: Delegated, reserved and concurrent powers get a modest graduated spread; none is treated as exceptional trivia.

categories.prompt: Name a form of federalism from our course.
categories.rationale: Dual and cooperative are direct course associations; fiscal and devolution models are less obvious.

categories.prompt: Name a type of congressional committee or committee arrangement.
categories.rationale: Standing committees are immediate; Rules, select and conference are more specific; joint and Committee of the Whole are less recalled.

categories.prompt: Name a congressional leadership position.
categories.rationale: Speaker and majority leaders are familiar; whips and presiding roles are less obvious.

categories.prompt: Name a presidential tool for carrying out policy.
categories.rationale: Veto and executive order are direct; pocket veto, agreements and signing statements require broader recall.

categories.prompt: Name a way Congress can check the president.
categories.rationale: Impeachment and veto override are immediate; treaty consent is less likely to be named first.

categories.prompt: Name a power the Senate has that the House does not.
categories.rationale: All three Senate-only powers are covered; confirmations are first recall, treaties next, trial of impeachments less immediate.

categories.prompt: Name a power the House has that the Senate does not.
categories.rationale: Impeachment is immediate, revenue bills less immediate, contingent election of the president least obvious.

answers.label: Choose the president in a contingent election

categories.prompt: Name a term about seats, district populations, or drawing district boundaries.
categories.rationale: Redistricting and gerrymandering are immediate; malapportionment and majority-minority districts are more specialized.

categories.prompt: Name a required Supreme Court case from Unit 1 or our districting lesson.
categories.rationale: Baker and McCulloch are familiar anchors; Shaw and Lopez require wider case recall.

categories.prompt: Name a U.S. president whose last name starts with M.
categories.rationale: Madison and Monroe are immediate M answers; McKinley is less obvious.

categories.prompt: Name a U.S. president whose last name starts with T.
categories.rationale: Trump and Truman are immediate T answers; Taft, Taylor and Tyler are progressively less recalled.

categories.prompt: Name a U.S. president whose last name starts with H.
categories.rationale: Hoover is an accessible H association; Hayes and the Harrisons remain larger rewards within this narrower category.

categories.prompt: Name a U.S. president whose last name starts with J.
categories.rationale: Jefferson and Jackson are immediate J associations; the Johnsons require more deliberate recall.

categories.prompt: Name a U.S. president whose last name starts with C.
categories.rationale: Clinton and Carter are familiar C answers; Cleveland and Coolidge are less immediate.

categories.prompt: Name a U.S. president whose last name starts with R.
categories.rationale: Reagan is an immediate R association; the Roosevelts earn modest larger steps within this small category.

categories.prompt: Name a U.S. president whose last name starts with B.
categories.rationale: Biden and George W. Bush are immediate; George H. W. Bush and Buchanan are less recalled.

categories.prompt: Name a U.S. president whose first name is James.
categories.rationale: Madison and Monroe are accessible; Polk, Buchanan and Garfield are progressively less recalled; James Carter is also accepted.

categories.prompt: Name a U.S. president whose first name is John.
categories.rationale: Kennedy and Adams are accessible; John Quincy Adams and Tyler require more recall.

categories.prompt: Name a U.S. president whose first name is William.
categories.rationale: Bill Clinton is accessible; Taft, McKinley and Harrison require more recall.

categories.prompt: Name a U.S. president whose first name is George.
categories.rationale: Washington is immediate; the two Bush administrations earn modest larger steps.

categories.prompt: Name one of the first five U.S. presidents.
categories.rationale: Washington and Jefferson are immediate; Adams, Madison and Monroe require more recall.

categories.prompt: Name one of the first ten U.S. presidents.
categories.rationale: Washington and Jefferson anchor the set; Van Buren, Harrison and Tyler are less recalled.

categories.prompt: Name a U.S. president who served at any time from January 1, 2000 through January 20, 2025.
categories.rationale: Recent presidents are immediate; earlier living former presidents are less obvious for this wording.

categories.prompt: Name a U.S. president who served at any time during the 1900s (1900–1999).
categories.rationale: Theodore Roosevelt and FDR anchor the century; Harding and Coolidge are less recalled.

categories.prompt: Name a U.S. president who took office before 1820.
categories.rationale: Washington and Jefferson are immediate; Adams, Madison and Monroe require broader recall for the birth-date wording.

categories.prompt: Name a U.S. president who also served as a U.S. senator.
categories.rationale: Biden and Obama are immediate recent associations; nineteenth-century Senate careers are less obvious.

categories.prompt: Name a U.S. president who also served as vice president.
categories.rationale: Biden is immediate; Adams, Jefferson and Roosevelt are accessible; lesser recalled succession paths earn more.

categories.prompt: Name a vice president who became president when the president died or resigned.
categories.rationale: Roosevelt, Truman and Johnson are accessible succession examples; Tyler, Fillmore and Arthur are less immediate.

categories.prompt: Name a president pictured on one of the seven current U.S. paper-money denominations.
categories.rationale: Washington and Lincoln are immediate; Grant is less likely to be recalled first.

categories.prompt: Name a U.S. president whose first name is John or James.
categories.rationale: Kennedy, Adams and Madison are accessible; Garfield, Buchanan and Tyler require broader recall.

categories.prompt: Name a U.S. president who served before Abraham Lincoln.
categories.rationale: Washington, Jefferson and Jackson anchor the set; lesser recalled early administrations earn more.

categories.prompt: Name a last name shared by more than one U.S. president.
categories.rationale: Bush is immediate; Adams and Roosevelt are accessible; Harrison is less obvious.

categories.prompt: Name a person pictured on one of the seven current U.S. paper-money denominations.
categories.rationale: Washington and Lincoln are immediate; Grant and Hamilton are less likely to be named first.

categories.prompt: Name a U.S. Cabinet department.
categories.rationale: Defense, Justice, Education and State are familiar; Interior, Commerce, Energy and HUD are less recalled.

answers.label: Department of Health and Human Services
Department of Housing and Urban Development

categories.prompt: Name an elected office in the U.S. federal government.
categories.rationale: All four are familiar; president and senator are the most immediate, with only modest extra reward for the others.

categories.prompt: Name a goal of government listed in the Constitution’s Preamble.
categories.rationale: Union and justice are immediate; domestic tranquility is less likely to be named first.

categories.prompt: Name one of the three authors of the Federalist Papers.
categories.rationale: Hamilton is immediate, Madison next, John Jay the less recalled contributor.

categories.prompt: Name a U.S. state that starts with A.
categories.rationale: Arizona and Alaska are accessible; Alabama and Arkansas earn progressively larger climbs.

categories.prompt: Name a U.S. state that starts with C.
categories.rationale: California is immediate for this classroom; Colorado next, Connecticut less obvious.

categories.prompt: Name a U.S. state that starts with I.
categories.rationale: Illinois and Indiana are accessible; Idaho and Iowa earn larger climbs.

categories.prompt: Name a U.S. state that starts with M.
categories.rationale: Michigan, Maryland and Massachusetts are accessible; Maine, Missouri and Montana are less immediate.

categories.prompt: Name a U.S. state that starts with N.
categories.rationale: New York is immediate; Nevada and New Jersey accessible; smaller northern/New England states less immediate.

categories.prompt: Name a U.S. state that starts with O.
categories.rationale: Ohio and Oregon are accessible; Oklahoma gets a modest larger reward.

categories.prompt: Name a U.S. state that starts with W.
categories.rationale: Washington and Wisconsin are accessible; West Virginia and Wyoming are less immediate.

categories.prompt: Name a formal constitutional power or duty of the president.
categories.rationale: Veto, signing and command are immediate; receiving ambassadors and special sessions are less recalled formal powers.

answers.label: Give the State of the Union

categories.prompt: Name an informal tool or power presidents use to shape policy.
categories.rationale: Executive order and public communication are familiar; agreements, agenda setting and signing statements are less immediate.

categories.prompt: Name a power of Congress.
categories.rationale: Passing laws, tax, war and impeachment are immediate; detailed Article I powers require broader recall.

answers.label: Punish piracy and offenses on the high seas
Punish offenses against the law of nations
Grant letters of marque and reprisal
Make rules for the armed forces
Organize and call forth the militia

categories.prompt: Name a chief executive position at the federal, state, or local level.
categories.rationale: President is immediate, governor next; mayor and local administration reward looking beyond the federal level.

categories.prompt: Name a legislative position at the federal, state, or local level.
categories.rationale: Members of Congress are immediate; state and local bodies and specialized leadership roles earn larger climbs.

categories.prompt: Name a key term or concept connected to Baker v. Carr.
categories.rationale: Equal protection and one person one vote are direct anchors; justiciability and political question doctrine are less obvious connections.

categories.prompt: Name a key term or concept connected to McCulloch v. Maryland.
categories.rationale: Necessary and Proper and implied powers are direct anchors; tax immunity and broader interpretive concepts are less obvious.

categories.prompt: Name a clause in the U.S. Constitution.
categories.rationale: Commerce, Supremacy and Necessary and Proper are familiar anchors; specialized clauses earn larger climbs.

categories.prompt: Name an office, power, rule, or idea discussed in Article I of the Constitution.
categories.rationale: Congress and its chambers, tax and war are immediate; procedural details and prohibitions are less recalled.

answers.label: Punish piracy and offenses on the high seas
Punish offenses against the law of nations
Grant letters of marque and reprisal
Make rules for the armed forces
Organize and call forth the militia
Revenue bills originate in the House

categories.prompt: Name an office, power, rule, or idea discussed in Article II of the Constitution.
categories.rationale: President and commander in chief are immediate; appointments and treaties accessible; specialized duties and qualifications less immediate.

answers.label: Adjourn Congress in a specified disagreement

categories.prompt: Name an office, power, rule, or idea discussed in Article III of the Constitution.
categories.rationale: Supreme Court and judicial power are immediate; specialized jurisdiction and treason requirements are less recalled.
